tags.gist: Applauds FDA for seeking comment first, agrees the paper correctly recognizes GenAI's distinctive risks, and wants the open iterative approach kept.
Wants the two axes to also weigh how constrained autonomy is, users' ability to catch errors, reversibility, population vulnerability and clinical context.
Finds the competency approach valuable if FDA turns capability into task-specific evidence expectations tied to intended use, user, setting and decision limits.
Wants benchmarking to cover difficult, out-of-distribution, incomplete, adversarial and ambiguous cases plus subgroup consistency, not only average performance.
Wants human factors evidence premarket: validated user safeguards, uncertainty communication, protection against overreliance, escalation and usability under time pressure.
Wants a traceability expectation covering the foundation model's lineage and version, prompts, orchestration, safety controls and validation of the final configuration.
Wants manufacturers of agentic systems to set enforceable autonomy limits, authorizations, oversight, audit records and safe fallback states.
Accepts risk-proportional monitoring but not as a substitute for adequate premarket proof in high-consequence applications.
Wants higher-risk devices to have a monitoring plan with data quality control, drift detection, thresholds, corrective actions and user communication, tied to existing obligations.
Wants PCCPs to specify bounded modifications, acceptance standards, verification, monitoring periods, rollback and user notification for foundation model and retrieval updates.
Wants FDA to pursue global convergence through IMDRF and regulators such as Health Canada and MHRA.
